answer.answer: PVE34 was a valid 10M-era fixed-profile result, not the final operating model. It proved that 64 fetch / 34 PVE / 2 PVP / 1 other workers could cross 10M cleanly at about 403/sec while preserving recovery and validation. Later autonomy work superseded worker-count fixation: current-code alpha exceeded 1k/sec, parser-owned S3 gamma exceeded 2k/sec, and workers/batches became evidence-driven, reversible controls. The next safe experiment is a bounded longer alpha soak using learned priors, full host-pressure telemetry and all integrity gates, preceded by a hard-kill/normal-restart proof; persistent controller learning should wait.

This established PVE34 as the best practical fixed Nyx profile for that data band and showed that DB/write coordination—not fetch or JSON—was limiting throughput despite substantial idle headroom. The later durable summary, created and updated `2026-05-25 08:55 PDT`, superseded fixed-profile tuning as the operating model. Fetch, DB-lane rebalance, batch, rollback, cooldown, and bad-trial decisions became active or shadow autoscaler decisions; workers can scale without closing shared queues and retire only after completing their current PGCR. Source-level `112` semantics were removed, fetch can reduce below `112` or to floor `4` at the slow edge and recover when present evidence shows underfeed, batch `128` is only the learned keeper-family ceiling, and DB rebalance is fixed-budget, one worker at a time, with acceptance or rollback and scenario-specific bad-trial memory. answer.answer: Prioritize `/in/playerActivity` outside the profile workstream. Its cache-miss path combines high traffic with a severe latency tail, and the existing five-minute refresh/TTL alignment lets foreground requests fall through to expensive Redis scanning. Implement stale-while-revalidate with a longer stale window and a single background rebuild. Separately, make `/p/:identifier/raids` render shell plus local raid results without waiting for Bungie collectibles, and defer Pantheon until its tab is selected or share the collectibles result server-side.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is `/in/playerActivity`, ranked first in the saved optimization candidates. Over seven days RUM recorded 13,210 analytics calls with avg 3.69 s, p75 1.09 s, and p95 12.03 s; APM recorded 23,255 exact `GET /in/playerActivity` spans with avg 1.99 s, p75 2 ms, and p95 13.03 s. The 2 ms APM p75 versus 13.03 s p95 identifies a fast cached majority and an extremely expensive miss tail, while 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs in 24 hours show that user requests are paying rebuild work.

Implement stale-while-revalidate for `apiPlayerActivity`: serve a last-known-good value through a longer stale TTL, refresh it in the background, and use a lock/single-flight guard so only one rebuild scans Redis. The code-path reason is that `apiPlayerActivity` reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache but falls back to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`, while `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` refreshes every 5 minutes with the same 5 minute TTL; any expiry or delayed sweep can therefore put the Redis scan on the foreground request path. Preserve the existing Discord behavior of treating a true cache absence as no-data rather than rebuilding synchronously.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie collectible enrichment rather than raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for all concurrent sources, including `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)`; meanwhile the route immediately starts a second Pantheon request that repeats `ProfileWCollectibles` before the Pantheon tab is opened. Change the route so shell identity plus fast local clears/full-clears/carries/fastest data renders the ready raid scaffold and cards first, then load collectible-dependent exotic, armor, triumph, guardian-rank/avatar enrichment separately. answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state and authoritative evidence. Obsidian/Markdown supply a prototype corpus, human projection, and export format; Metis is the knowledge-base system, while Straylight is the agent continuity product. The first benchmark measured retrieval readiness rather than the product’s core outcome. The expanded evaluation must show that a fresh agent can correctly resume, advance, verify, compute over, and durably hand off real work.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer: an agent-first product and protocol for durable machine continuity across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval system, or memory database.

Beyond learned knowledge, Straylight must preserve the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and resumable next actions. The workspace must let a later agent inspect provenance and prior state, reopen and query the work, compute over it, revise it as evidence changes, verify it, checkpoint it, and leave a better versioned durable state for the next agent. Full source artifacts and evidence remain available; summaries, embeddings, indexes, and context packs are derived aids rather than truth boundaries, and task checkpoints are refreshed independently from durable semantic-memory promotion.

Obsidian is not the product boundary because Metis and its vault organize the human knowledge base, whereas Straylight is the portable agent context and durable-work product designed over such corpora. Obsidian and Markdown are useful prototype and evaluation inputs, human-readable projections, and export formats, but raw Markdown is neither assumed to be the only or canonical storage representation nor the canonical interaction model; Straylight’s primary interaction model is agent-first.

The first benchmark was too narrow because it was a retrieval-readiness test: 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items compared direct full-file access, one-shot BM25 top-k, and a minimal deterministic Memory Workspace across Metis, N24 RaceWatch, Home Network Improvements, and Straylight. Policy 0.2 and one-shot top-k each passed 17 of 20 cases, while one-shot recovered 48 of 53 evidence items versus 46 of 53 for the workspace and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932; model-directed `memory.compute` and `memory.verify` remained untested, so the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated. Retrieval-only scoring is now a regression lane. The expanded primary evaluation must compare direct filesystem search/range reads/scripts, an agent-first workspace using model-directed `open`, `query`, `read`, `compute`, `verify`, checkpoint, and revision behavior, and fixed handoff/context packs. On untouched, blinded real-work cases, it must prove that a fresh agent can resume, iterate after changing constraints, inspect full sources, reason over time, supersession and contradictions, perform quantitative artifact work, verify before acting, continue incidents, and leave correct durable next-state artifacts. Required workloads are Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture planning, Switzerland trip planning including booked-versus-proposed state, and Straylight’s own evolution. No canonical storage-engine decision is justified until that gate tests model-directed workspace calls against an untouched holdout set.
